author: Steve Clark
title: 'Heart of our community': Four-year journey leads to Harlingen VFW groundbreaking - NewsBreak
text:
By Steve Clark ,
1 days ago
H ARLINGEN — Inside VFW Post 2410 at midday on Monday, it was quiet and mostly empty, just a couple of guys sitting at the bar and a young woman behind it washing glasses.
Outside, it was anything but quiet. Dozens of veterans and family members, dignitaries, law enforcement and regular folks milled about in a festive atmosphere under a bright blue sky, enjoying a pleasant northerly breeze while waiting for the start of the official groundbreaking ceremony for the historic post’s new home.
Whataburger had set up an orange-and-white striped tent where breakfast sandwiches were being handed out for free. H-E-B was on hand with a tent of its own. Music from the Moises V. Vela Middle School band filled the air, while an enormous American flag flew from the top of a Harlingen Fire Department ladder truck.
It took four years to arrive at this day.
A computer rendering shows what the new VFW Post 2410 building in Harlingen will look like once complete. (Courtesy: Noble Texas Builders) During the pandemic, Noble Texas Builders president and CEO Rene Capistran happened to see a TV news story about Post 2410 that he assumed was going to be an inspiring, feel-good piece, though it wasn’t. It turned out that the post, founded in 1939 and active in community service for decades, was watching its 70-year-old-plus, patched-together, flood-prone headquarters on North Whalen Road fall apart around it.
Capistran, a Navy veteran, was invited to tour the facility. His verdict as a professional builder — to the dismay of many of the post’s members — was that it was too far gone to save. He decided the post was going to get a new home and it wouldn’t cost them a dime. Capistran called up his friend U.S. Rep. Vicente Gonzalez, D-Brownsville, who secured $850,000 for the roughly $2.5 million project. Cameron County kicked in another $150,000.
When the dust had settled, more than two dozen Noble subcontractors and suppliers had stepped up with pledges of materials, labor and/or services, much of it pledged during Noble Charity’s seventh annual fishing tournament. The project’s partners and in-kind contributors numbered more than 30. During the ceremony Gonzalez presented each with a framed, folded American flag flown over the U.S. Capitol.
“As a community, we have a moral responsibility to come together as one for those who have done so much for our country,” Capistran said in his remarks on stage. “Today this project stands as proof of what can happen when people unite behind a common purpose. But these things don’t happen by themselves.”
He expressed gratitude to those “critical to this mission,” starting with Gonzalez.
“Thank you, brother, because you answered my call four years ago,” Capistran said. “You came down here and walked around, and more importantly, you helped us secure the money that we needed to cover that gap. So thank you for your leadership.”
To help further close the funding gap, he next called on Cameron County Precinct 4 Commissioner Gus Ruiz, a Marine Corps veteran, and County Judge Eddie Treviño Jr.
“Immediately, they stepped up and said, we’re there,” Capistran said. “You all came and toured the facility along with my brothers and sisters from the VFW and said yes.”
A view of VFW Post 2410 in Harlingen on Tuesday, May 5, 2026. (Miguel Roberts/The Brownsville Herald) He praised Noble’s many suppliers and subcontractors who helped make it a reality, also thanking Harlingen Mayor Norma Sepulveda and City Manager Gabriel Gonzalez for their support.
“You all stood side by side from the very day that we talked about this facility, and (the city) donated the building permit,” Capistran said. “We had to go through a very long process to get this facility permitted, but the city of Harlingen was there and immediately said yes. It takes a village. This is what it means, ladies and gentlemen.”
Gonzalez, taking his turn at the podium, said the way so many different partners came together to make the project a reality should serve as a model and that he was proud to be a part of it.
“This is a real example to the rest of the country of when a community comes together to do what’s right, to do what’s right for our veterans, to create a space that’s going to be transformative for our community,” he said. “It’s going to be transformative for families, a place for veterans to hang out with each other, console each other.”
VFW halls are spaces for veterans’ families just as much as the veterans themselves, Gonzalez noted.
“We have birthday parties, we celebrate quinceañeras, we celebrate all different types of events,” he said. “VFWs are … the heart of our community, and they bring us together.”
Observing that many VFW posts around the country are in the same boat when it comes to the condition of their buildings, Gonzalez insisted he intends to keep pushing for federal funds to do as much as he can to fix it.
“These VFWs were built mostly during World War II, and many of them haven’t been touched since,” he said.
A groundbreaking ceremony was held Monday, May 11, 2026, in Harlingen for the VFW Post 2410’s new facility. (Courtesy: City of Harlingen /Facebook) Ruiz, in his remarks, said it was a “no-brainer” for the county to hop onboard the Post 2410 project, and invited all local veterans of foreign wars to enjoy the building once it’s complete.
The new, 10,000-square-foot facility will be built next to the existing structure, which will be demolished for parking after the post has moved into its new digs.
Treviño, taking the stage, said that once Capistran committed himself to seeing the project through, it was an easy decision for the county get behind it.
“The reality is that in Cameron County, for every dollar we have, there’s about $100,000 worth of need, and it’s hard to stretch that dollar to meet that, but we do everything we possibly can,” Treviño said. “Ladies and gentlemen, it’s an honor and a privilege to be part of this process.”
The actual groundbreaking is scheduled for May 25 and construction is expected to take 10 months to complete.
